meta.description: Edit phylogenetic tree structure with Biopython Bio.Phylo, treating rooting as a separate statistical inference rather than a display choice.
meta.audit_type: final pass regression of all eight archived scenario areas plus two fresh inputs
meta.execution_note: 31/31 assertions passed with Biopython 1.88. Archived synthetic trees exercised close-outgroup rooting, pruning, dual-label collapse, MAD, MinVar, LBA detection, and IQ-TREE 3 non-reversible root confidence; the archived scope-boundary item was evaluated as a routing answer.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All empirical claims in this pass use archived synthetic trees or explicitly labelled tool output; the Skill refuses unsupported basal and dated claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research tree editing only; no clinical or individual diagnostic claim.

methodological_ground.detail: The separate a-priori ingroup check is executable in both the documented snippet and the shipped root example, preventing an outgroup-complement tautology.

code_usability.detail: All five shipped examples compile and run from a clean working directory under Biopython 1.88.

functional_suitability.note: Rooting, pruning, collapse, induced-subtree, and distance examples have executable coverage.

reliability.note: Outgroup and ingroup checks, dual-label support parsing, and no-readable-support guard cover prior silent failures.

performance_context.note: The 247-line main Skill keeps structural edits local and directs heavyweight inference to dedicated tools.

agent_usability.note: Rooting decision table and explicit routes distinguish editing from inference and dating.

human_usability.note: Failure modes state the consequence and recovery for LBA, rate variation, branch lengths, and polytomies.

security.note: Examples use local files and no credential, network, or shell-evaluation path.

maintainability.note: Five small runnable examples align with the core instructions and version checks.

agent_specific.note: Trigger, scope boundaries, and tool routing are precise; specialised command availability still needs environment verification.
